description.purpose: Search across Stripe customers, charges, and subscriptions by free-text query and return ranked smart IDs.
when_to_use: When the user asks to find a Stripe object by partial name, email, or amount.
When the user does not know the exact object ID and wants the most relevant matches first.
when_not_to_use: When the exact ID is already known — use `fetch` instead.
When the user wants every object in a collection — use `list_objects` with a filter.
limitations: Returns at most 25 results per call; use `list_objects` with pagination for full enumeration.
No fuzzy matching on amounts; numeric matches are exact only.
Index lag of up to 60s for newly created objects.
description.parameter_overview: Single `query` string; the server fans out to /v1/charges, /v1/customers, /v1/subscriptions and returns ranked smart IDs of the form stripe-prod-stripe:object:Customer:cus_...

query.description: Free-text search query (email, name, partial ID, or description fragment).

truncation.guidance_template: Showing {N} of {Total} matches. Use `cursor` to paginate or refine your query to narrow the result set.

description.purpose: Fetch the full Stripe object addressed by a smart ID (Customer, Charge, Subscription, Refund).
when_to_use: When you already have a smart ID returned by `search` or `list_objects`.
When you need the full object payload (not just the search-ranked preview).
limitations: Returns the full object — may be large; use `properties` filter on `list_objects` for projection.
404 if the object was deleted or never existed.
description.parameter_overview: Single `id` string in the smart-ID format `stripe-prod-stripe:object:{Customer|Charge|Subscription|Refund}:{stripe_id}`; routing maps the type to the correct Stripe endpoint.

truncation.guidance_template: Object exceeded {threshold} tokens; {N} fields included. Request specific fields via `properties` on a list-style call to project.

description.purpose: List the available top-level Stripe object collections (Customer, Charge, Subscription, Refund) for discovery.
when_to_use: At the start of a session to discover what kinds of data the Stripe MCP exposes.
When mapping a user request to the right object type for `list_objects` or `search`.
limitations: Returns metadata only — no records. Use `list_objects` to enumerate within a collection.
description.parameter_overview: Optional `pattern` (glob) and `include_schema` (bool) for filtering and schema inclusion respectively; defaults return all collections without schema.

truncation.guidance_template: Listed {N} collections. Use `pattern` to narrow the listing if needed.

description.purpose: List Stripe objects within a chosen collection with optional filtering, sorting, and projection.
when_to_use: When the user wants to enumerate objects of a known type (e.g. all subscriptions for a customer).
When you need pagination, server-side filtering, or a projected subset of fields.
when_not_to_use: When the user has a known ID — use `fetch` instead.
When the user is unsure which collection — use `search` instead.
limitations: Cursor pagination only; no offset.
Filter expressions limited to fields exposed by the upstream Stripe list endpoint.
Max 100 records per call.
description.parameter_overview: `collection` (required) names the object type. `filter` is a structured object `{property, operator, value}`. `properties` projects fields. `sort_by`/`sort_order` order results. `limit` and `cursor` paginate.

truncation.guidance_template: Returned {N} of approximately {Total} {collection} objects (truncated at {threshold} tokens). Use `cursor` to paginate or `properties` to project fewer fields.

description.purpose: Create a new Stripe object or update an existing one within the chosen collection (smart routing by presence of id).
when_to_use: When inserting a single new Customer, Charge, or Subscription.
When updating mutable fields on an existing object by smart ID.
limitations: Stripe Charges are not idempotent on retry without an Idempotency-Key — caller must supply one.
Subscriptions cannot be re-created with the same id (Stripe rejects).
Batch upsert (ids array) is sequential — partial failure leaves earlier successes committed.
description.parameter_overview: `collection` selects the type. Provide `data` alone to create; provide `id` + `data` to update. Optional `idempotency_key` (recommended for Charge create) for safe retries.

truncation.guidance_template: Object {action} succeeded; full payload returned. If response exceeded {threshold}, refetch with `properties` projection.

description.purpose: Delete one Stripe object, a batch of objects, or empty a collection (smart routing by `type` discriminator).
when_to_use: When the user explicitly asks to permanently delete a Customer, Charge, or Subscription.
When cleanup is required before a fresh import.
when_not_to_use: When canceling a Subscription — use the dedicated `subscriptions_cancel` action (preserves audit trail and proration semantics).
When refunding a Charge — use `charges_refund` instead (delete is not supported on Charge).
limitations: Charge cannot be deleted via API; use `charges_refund` for reversal.
Deletion is irreversible. The `confirm` flag MUST be true.
Batch delete is sequential.
description.parameter_overview: `type` is one of `object|objects|collection`. Provide `id` for single, `ids` for batch, `collection` for full sweep. `confirm: true` is mandatory; the call refuses without it.

truncation.guidance_template: Deleted {deleted_count} of {requested} objects. Re-call with the remaining IDs if needed; deletion is idempotent.

description.purpose: Capture the funds previously authorized on an uncaptured Charge so the payment settles to the merchant.
when_to_use: When the merchant created a Charge with `capture: false` and now wants to settle it.
When applying a partial capture (capture less than the authorized amount).
limitations: Charge must currently be in `pending` capture status; otherwise returns 400.
Once captured, cannot be uncaptured — only refunded.
Authorization windows differ per card brand (typically 7 days).
description.parameter_overview: Required smart `id` of the Charge (`stripe-prod-stripe:object:Charge:ch_...`). Optional `amount` to capture a partial amount; defaults to the full authorized amount.

truncation.guidance_template: Captured charge {id} for amount {amount}. Use `fetch` to retrieve the full updated Charge object if needed.

description.purpose: Refund a previously captured Charge fully or partially (issues funds back to the original payment method).
when_to_use: When a customer requests a refund on a settled Charge.
When automating returns or chargeback prevention.
limitations: Cannot refund more than the captured amount.
Refund is destructive — cannot be reversed.
Refunding pending Charges fails with 400; capture first.
description.parameter_overview: Required `charge_id` (smart ID of the source Charge). Optional `amount` for partial refund (default: full). Optional `reason` enum (duplicate / fraudulent / requested_by_customer).

truncation.guidance_template: Refund {id} created for charge {charge}. Status {status}; reason {reason}. Final settlement may take 5-10 business days.

description.purpose: Cancel an active Subscription so no further invoices are issued (idempotent — re-canceling is a no-op).
when_to_use: When the user requests an immediate cancellation.
When churn workflows trigger end-of-period cancellation (set `at_period_end: true`).
limitations: Cannot un-cancel — must create a new Subscription.
Re-canceling a canceled Subscription is a no-op (returns the same canceled object).
Proration behavior governed by `prorate` flag (default true).
description.parameter_overview: Required `id` (smart ID of Subscription). Optional `at_period_end: true` defers cancellation to the next billing date. Optional `prorate: false` disables proration.

truncation.guidance_template: Subscription {id} canceled. Final invoice will issue on {ended_at} (or now if at_period_end=false).
